items.author: Lee Harris
items.text:
A remarkable and deeply moving photograph capturing the first two minutes of silence in London, 106 years ago on Tuesday 11th November 1919. 

The first time a grieving nation held its collective breath.

Lest we forget.

items.author: Keri Smith 🌱Deprogrammed
items.text:
If you are feeling nothing but doom, let me tell you about one of the blessings of a good church, with a strong Pastor and elders, rooted in the word. 

Our Pastor @BradleyJHelger1’s sermon today was about the 3 reasons for God’s judgment of a nation, and the various steps we should take following judgment. The first among them being repentance. 

But the take away was that our response is never despair. Despair wasn’t the response of our forefathers. It wasn’t the response of our nation’s founders. And it’s not the Christian response. We build and we fight. The trowel and the sword. 

I’ll share the sermon when it’s up. If you don’t have a strong church family, find one. Build one. There’s nothing else like it. 🙏🔥

items.author: David Senra
items.text:
Palo Alto Networks’ @nikesharora believes cybersecurity is actually very simple:

1. Stop bad guys at the perimeter.
2. Keep the inside of the house in order.
3. Assume something will get through: find it and eject it before it can do harm.

“That's cybersecurity in a nutshell.”

items.author: anu
items.text: “Make it exist first, then you can make it good” is one of those nice sayings that’s meant to help you overcome inertia and perfectionism, but following this advice too bluntly is risky. Because once you make something exist, it’s tempting to focus next on making it *grow*. And by then you’re already trapped in the iteration you’ve shipped first, at least for a while.

items.author: Matt Ahlborg
items.text:
We @PPQdotAI use a TEE router. It makes it so that we:

1) Cannot see the content of our users’ queries
2) Prove the model and provider that the query ended up executing (no model fraud possible)

Other routers follow the “trust me bro” architecture.
